title: Authentication and Password Storage
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of authentication and password storage in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply authentication and password storage in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to avoiding homemade cryptographic designs and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Authentication and Password Storage through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding authentication and password storage helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Authentication and Password Storage helps you reason about authentication versus authorization. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Authentication versus authorization. Then connect it to Established password-hashing libraries. The remaining syllabus points—Password reset and session concepts, Avoiding homemade cryptographic designs—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Authentication and Password Storage
content_blocks.code:
def valid_username?(value)
  value.is_a?(String) && value.match?(/\A[a-z0-9_]{3,20}\z/i)
end
puts valid_username?("learner_7")
puts valid_username?("bad name")

content_blocks.title: Guided example
